sans.purpose: Geist. All interface chrome: buttons, badges, form controls, nav, labels. The default UI voice.

heading.purpose: Geist via font-heading. Page titles, dialog/sheet/card titles, section headings such as the note details sheet's Review history, empty-state headings.

reading.purpose: var(--reading-font): Geist by default, Literata when the device picks serif in Settings → Appearance. Only note titles and note bodies.

serif.purpose: The serif option behind the reading font, plus the Appearance setting's preview. Never hard-coded on content.

mono.purpose: Geist Mono. Code blocks, inline code, CodeMirror content, API token display, JSON import preview.

shadows.name: floating-overlay
shadows.purpose: Popover, select dropdown, and combobox dropdown — always paired with ring-1 ring-foreground/10. Never used on docked/inline surfaces like cards or dialogs.

shadows.name: ambient-sidebar
shadows.purpose: The sidebar's rare floating variant and the inset main-content area — a softer touch than the overlay shadow.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default button variant — green-ink fill, used for the main affirmative action on a page or dialog.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.25rem; height: 1.75rem; padding: 0 0.5rem; border-radius: 0.6rem; border: 1px solid transparent; font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1.625; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary, oklch(0.52 0.12 152)); color: var(--primary-foreground, oklch(0.99 0.005 85)); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary, oklch(0.52 0.12 152)) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring, oklch(0.62 0.11 152)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.62 0.11 152)) 30%, transparent); outline: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Quiet-fill button for secondary actions alongside a primary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: var(--secondary, oklch(0.955 0.006 85)); color: var(--secondary-foreground, oklch(0.52 0.12 152)); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--secondary, oklch(0.955 0.006 85)), var(--foreground, oklch(0.21 0.012 60)) 5%); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Transparent at rest, filled with a muted tint on hover — the low-emphasis action button.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.21 0.012 60)); border-color: var(--border, oklch(0.905 0.007 85)); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--input, oklch(0.905 0.007 85)), transparent 50%); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Low-opacity red fill rather than a solid red button — restrained semantic color, matching the badge system's treatment.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)), transparent 90%); color: var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)), transparent 80%); }

components.name: Difficulty Badge
components.description: Pill-shaped status chip — the system's primary carrier of semantic color. This instance shows the 'hard' difficulty variant; easy/medium/good/again follow the same shape with emerald/amber/blue/red tints respectively.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 1.25rem; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 0.625rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-badge-hard { background: color-mix(in oklch, oklch(0.63 0.2 25), transparent 85%); color: oklch(0.5 0.2 25); }

components.name: Outline Badge (tag chip)
components.description: Interactive tag/project chip — outline variant, clickable, filters the note list on click.
components.css: .ds-badge-outline { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--input, oklch(0.905 0.007 85)), transparent 80%); color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.21 0.012 60)); border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.905 0.007 85)); cursor: pointer; } .ds-badge-outline:hover { background: var(--muted, oklch(0.955 0.006 85)); }

components.name: Note Card
components.description: Signature component: fixed-height card so grid rows stay aligned regardless of content length, with a stretched-link title and a bottom gradient fade signaling clipped overflow.
components.html:
Segment tree

Range queries in O(log n)...

Hard
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 18rem; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 0.75rem; background: var(--card, oklch(0.995 0.002 85)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--foreground, oklch(0.21 0.012 60)), transparent 90%); font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1.625; } .ds-card-header { padding: 1rem 1rem 0; } .ds-card-title { font-family: var(--reading-font, 'Geist Variable', sans-serif); font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.21 0.012 60)); } .ds-card-content { position: relative; flex: 1; min-height: 0; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; overflow: hidden; font-family: var(--reading-font, 'Geist Variable', sans-serif); } .ds-card-fade { position: absolute; inset-inline: 0; bottom: 0; height: 2rem; background: linear-gradient(to top, var(--card, oklch(0.995 0.002 85)), transparent); pointer-events: none; } .ds-card-footer { padding: 0 1rem 1rem; display: flex; gap: 0.375rem; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Compact translucent-fill input, the default form control across the app.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 1.75rem; width: 100%; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 0.6rem; border: 1px solid var(--input, oklch(0.905 0.007 85)); background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--input, oklch(0.905 0.007 85)), transparent 80%); font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.21 0.012 60)); outline: none; transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.52 0.012 70)); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring, oklch(0.62 0.11 152)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.62 0.11 152)) 30%, transparent); }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Flat icon+label nav item; hover uses the neutral sidebar-accent, the active item takes a primary/10 green tint with primary text and medium weight.
components.html: Home
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; width: 100%; padding: 0.5rem; border-radius: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--sidebar-foreground, oklch(0.21 0.012 60)); text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--sidebar-accent, oklch(0.955 0.006 85)); } .ds-nav-item-active { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary, oklch(0.52 0.12 152)) 10%, transparent); font-weight: 500; color: var(--primary, oklch(0.52 0.12 152)); }

narrative.overview:
Notes Again is a single-user tool, not a marketing surface, and its design reads that way on purpose: a compact working notebook of warm paper and green ink rather than a SaaS dashboard. The neutral scale is never cold gray — background, borders, and text all carry a faint warm paper tint (~60–85° hue, chroma ≤ 0.012), and the green (~152°) is reserved for ink: the primary action, the active nav item, focus, links, selection. Keeping green off the surfaces is what lets it read as meaning; an earlier version tinted every neutral with the accent hue and the whole app felt damp and gray-green. Surfaces sit flat against that paper-toned background, separated by hairline rings rather than shadows; shadow is reserved for the handful of things that genuinely float above the page (popovers, selects, comboboxes).

Density is deliberately tight — 28px controls, 12px base UI text, compact spacing — because this is a tool its one user operates dozens of times a day, not a surface meant to feel spacious for a first-time visitor. Type is one family, Geist, for the whole interface, with a single role split: the user's own notes (a note's title wherever it appears, and its body) render in the *reading font*, a per-device setting that is Geist by default or Literata serif for a more book-like page. Everything else — page titles, section headings, buttons, badges, dialogs, empty states — is interface and stays in Geist regardless of that setting.
keyCharacteristics: One accent hue (~152°, green ink) carries primary, ring, active nav, links, and selection; neutrals are warm paper (~85°), never tinted with the accent.
Flat-by-default: hairline ring (`ring-1 ring-foreground/10`) defines containers; shadow is reserved for floating overlays.
Geist for the interface; the reading font (Geist or Literata, chosen per device in Settings → Appearance) only for note titles and note bodies.
Dense, compact control sizing (28px controls, 12px base text) suited to a power-user tool used many times a day.
Pill-shaped badges carry all semantic status color (difficulty, recall rating, tags, project) rather than color on text or backgrounds elsewhere.

rules.name: The Paper and Ink Rule
rules.body: Surfaces, lines, and text are warm paper neutrals; green is ink and appears only where it means action, selection, or focus. Never tint a surface or neutral with the accent hue, and never spend green on decoration. A new color that isn't a deliberate semantic break (destructive red, difficulty/rating chips) is either a paper step or a green step.

rules.name: The Reading Font Rule
rules.body: Only the user's notes take `font-reading`: a note's title and its body, wherever they appear (card, table row, detail page, review session, trash). Everything else is interface and takes Geist (`font-sans` / `font-heading`), so switching the reading font changes the notes and nothing around them. Never hard-code Literata (`font-serif`) on content; it exists for the Appearance setting's preview.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface docked in the normal document flow (card, dialog, sidebar) gets a ring, never a shadow. Shadow is earned only by floating above unrelated content.

dos: Do put note titles and note bodies in `font-reading` and everything else, page titles included, in Geist — see The Reading Font Rule.

Do define container depth with a hairline ring (`ring-1 ring-foreground/10`) at rest; add `shadow-md` only when a surface floats above unrelated page content (popover, select, combobox) — see The Flat-By-Default Rule.
Do carry semantic status (difficulty, recall rating, tags) as badge fills, not colored text or full-color solid backgrounds elsewhere.
Do keep surfaces and neutrals on warm paper and spend green only on action, selection, and focus — see The Paper and Ink Rule.
Do compensate for the deliberately compact (20–32px) control sizing with the `(pointer: coarse)` media query rather than growing controls for every user.
donts: Don't add a second UI accent hue; route new emphasis through green ink at a different lightness/chroma, or through the established destructive/difficulty/rating palettes.
Don't put shadows on resting cards, dialogs, or the docked sidebar — that breaks the flat-by-default elevation model this system is built on.
Don't hard-code a face on note content (`font-serif`, `font-sans`) or apply `font-reading` to interface chrome — the reading font is the user's setting for their notes only.

Don't treat this as a marketing/persuade surface (no hero imagery, no decorative illustration, no gradient-heavy visual language) — it's a personal utility tool and its restraint is intentional, not a placeholder waiting for "real" design.
